facts.text: Ellsworth sprang from a coal boom when James Ellsworth built a shaft mine and coke yard in 1900, later selling the mines to Bethlehem Steel in the 1920s.
The town’s first mine, a large shaft and coke yard, opened in 1900 under the James Ellsworth Coal Co., giving Ellsworth its name.
Bethlehem Mines kept mining at Ellsworth until 1982, making it one of the longest‑running coal operations in the region.
Ellsworth’s brick “coal patch” houses stand out because they are single‑family structures, unlike the common two‑family miner homes elsewhere.
Just beyond Ellsworth’s edge, the Lithuanian Club—along with Polish, Italian, and Slovak clubs—highlights the town’s early 1900s European immigrant heritage.
When photographed in 2003, the Ellsworth power house and boiler house were still standing, a reminder of the town’s industrial past.
